topics.label: Introduction to the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and outlines how previously learned concepts will be integrated.

topics.label: Principles of innate sensing via PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental requirements and cellular localization strategies used by pattern recognition receptors to detect conserved microbial products and signs of tissue damage.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific receptor systems including toll-like receptors, cytoplasmic sensors, and the inflammasome complex that coordinate downstream inflammatory signaling.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated tissue sentinel cells stimulate endothelial adhesion molecules and chemokine gradients to guide circulating leukocytes into infected tissue.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how fluid drainage through the lymphatic system enables dendritic cells to transport antigens to lymph nodes for adaptive immune activation.

topics.label: Pathology of excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the severe physiological consequences and high mortality associated with uncontrolled systemic cytokine release during sepsis.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the passive and active mechanisms that terminate inflammation, drive wound healing and scar formation, and lead to persistent adaptations such as granulomas.

topics.label: Conclusion of the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic marks the conclusion of the session and previews the subject of the upcoming lecture.
